<description>
The `torcontrol` fuzz target hands made-up replies straight to the `TorController` callbacks, and caps each reply line at 16 characters. As a result:

- Most success paths can't be reached. They need lines such as `AUTH METHODS=...`, `ServiceID=<v3 id>` or `net/listeners/socks=...`.
- The code that parses bytes from the control port (`ProcessBuffer`, `ReceiveAndProcess`) and the command/reply chain are never fuzzed.

This PR adds:

- Allows reply lines up to 256 characters.
- Builds the values the fuzzer can't produce on its own:
  - v3 onion IDs, which need a checksum;
  - well-formed private keys;
  - `AUTH` lines that point at cookie files created for the test;
  - SAFECOOKIE server hashes.
- Drives a real `TorControlConnection` over a `DynSock`, with the harness playing Tor. This covers split writes, CRLF/LF line endings, async replies, EOF and reconnects. Direct handler calls are kept, so deep paths stay cheap to reach.
- Asserts that every command sent to Tor starts with a known command name and contains no stray line break.
- Keeps the target deterministic:
  - seeds the RNG;
  - clears `mapLocalHost` before each input;
  - only lets `COOKIEFILE` name files the harness created, so Tor input can't make the node read arbitrary host files.

The first commit fixes `DynSock::Wait()`. It wrapped `this` in an owning `shared_ptr`, so the socket deleted itself when the call returned. The bug has been there since #30205 and only showed up once this target called `Wait()`.

Coverage of `src/torcontrol.cpp`:

|        | lines | branches |
|--------|------:|---------:|
| master | 52.2% | 47.5% |
| this PR | 81.8% | 74.0% |

The master numbers come from the current qa-assets corpus. The numbers for this PR come from a short local run starting from the same seeds.

This changes the input format, so the qa-assets corpus for this target needs a refresh. I would be happy to open a a PR on qa-assets with new minimized corpus for this target.
</description>
